skeleton.description: Fetch all Gmail Inbox messages from the last 3 days and save them as structured JSON files.

state.name: preflight
state.contract:
Check that all four required environment variables are present and non-empty: GMAIL_CLIENT_ID, GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET, GMAIL_REDIRECT_URI, GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN.
If any variable is absent or empty, emit a clear error message listing every missing variable name (do NOT print the value of any credential var), then return FAIL.
If all four are present return PASS.
No files are written by this stage.

state.name: list_messages
state.contract:
Initialise a googleapis OAuth2 client using GMAIL_CLIENT_ID, GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET, GMAIL_REDIRECT_URI, and GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN from process.env, then instantiate the Gmail v1 client (the googleapis SDK handles token refresh automatically).
Compute the 3-day cutoff as: cutoff = Math.floor((Date.now() - 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) / 1000) (Unix epoch seconds).
Call gmail.users.messages.list with: userId = 'me', labelIds = ['INBOX'], q = `after:${cutoff}`, maxResults = 500. Repeat with pageToken = nextPageToken until nextPageToken is absent. Coerce a missing messages field to [] on every page.
Collect all {id, threadId} stubs into a flat array.
Write the array to own output directory as `message_ids.json` (valid JSON array; empty array if no messages were found).
Emit to console the total count of message IDs collected.
If the OAuth token exchange fails or any API call returns a non-2xx error, emit a clear human-readable error message (do NOT include the value of GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET or GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN in any log line or file) and return FAIL.
Return DONE on success (including the zero-messages case).

state.name: fetch_and_save
state.contract:
Read `message_ids.json` from the list_messages stage output directory.
If the array is empty: write `inbox-summary.json` containing the JSON literal `[]` to own output directory, emit "0 messages downloaded", and return DONE.
Otherwise, re-initialise the googleapis OAuth2 + Gmail v1 client from env vars (same as list_messages).
Fetch full message details in parallel batches of ≤ 20 using gmail.users.messages.get({ userId: 'me', id, format: 'full' }). Wait for each batch to settle before starting the next, and insert a 50 ms delay between batches to stay within quota (250 units/user/second). Emit console progress after each batch (e.g. "Fetched 20/143…").
For each raw message response, extract and assemble a record: - id : message.id - threadId : message.threadId - from : From header value, or "(unknown)" if absent - to : To header value, or "(unknown)" if absent - subject : Subject header value, or "(no subject)" if absent - date : Date header value parsed to an ISO 8601 string; fall back to new Date(Number(message.internalDate)).toISOString() if the Date header is absent or unparseable - snippet : message.snippet - bodyText : decoded UTF-8 string — prefer text/plain part; if none exists fall back to the first text/html part (stored as raw HTML); if neither exists use empty string "" - bodyMimeType : "text/plain" or "text/html" depending on which part was used; omit the field when bodyText is "" - labelIds : message.labelIds array
Decoding base64url: replace '-' → '+' and '_' → '/', then Buffer.from(data, 'base64').toString('utf-8'). bodyText must never be a raw base64url string.
For multipart payloads, recurse into payload.parts[] to find the preferred text/plain leaf; if not found recurse again for text/html.
Write each assembled record as `<id>.json` to own output directory.
After all messages are written, build a summary array containing one entry per message with fields {id, threadId, from, to, subject, date, snippet} and write it as `inbox-summary.json` (valid JSON array) to own output directory. The summary record count must equal the number of per-message JSON files written.
Emit to console the final count and the date range (earliest and latest message date) covered.
Prohibited: do NOT include the values of GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET or GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN in any output file or log line.
Return DONE on success. Return FAIL if any messages.get call fails with a non-retriable error (emit a clear message identifying the failing message ID and HTTP status).
